introduction.situation: Chemistry studies substances, from single atoms to biological macromolecules and applied materials.
introduction.complication: Chemical knowledge is recorded in many overlapping schemes, so topics about the same substance are scattered by source rather than by the question being asked.
introduction.question: How is everything chemistry knows about a substance divided?
introduction.answer: Chemistry is divided by the question asked of a substance, from what it is to how it is made or found: composition and identity, structure and bonding, equilibrium and energy, rates and mechanisms, and synthesis and analysis.

governing_thought: Chemistry is divided by the question asked of a substance, from what it is to how it is made or found: composition and identity, structure and bonding, equilibrium and energy, rates and mechanisms, and synthesis and analysis.

key_line.mece_dimension: the question asked of a substance
key_line.rank_note: The questions run from what a substance is, through how it is arranged and how it changes, to how it is made or found.

points.title: Composition and identity

points.name: Composition and identity is the question of what a substance is, covering its general kind, its compound class and its role.

points.name: Biochemical substances are classes of compounds defined by the role they play in living systems.

points.statement: Elemental, inorganic, biological and organic identity questions ask which elements and which kinds of molecule a substance consists of.
points.name: Elemental, inorganic, biological and organic identity questions ask which elements and which kinds of molecule a substance consists of.

points.name: Fields that ask which elements make up a substance and how those elements, by chemical family, behave.

points.name: Fields that ask what a material or molecular assembly is made of and how its structure and internal motion are organised.

points.name: Macromolecular and materials chemistry not elsewhere classified

points.name: Fields that ask how a material can be conceived and designed in theory to achieve desired properties, and how it behaves in aggregate.

points.statement: Fields that ask how a substance behaves under computation, quantum theory and its interaction with radiation.
points.name: Fields that ask how a substance behaves under computation, quantum theory and its interaction with radiation.

points.statement: Theoretical and computational chemistry not elsewhere classified
points.name: Theoretical and computational chemistry not elsewhere classified

points.title: Equilibrium and energy
points.statement: Equilibrium and energy is the question of how a substance exchanges energy, charge and matter and settles between states, phases and surroundings.
points.name: Equilibrium and energy is the question of how a substance exchanges energy, charge and matter and settles between states, phases and surroundings.

support.rank_note: From internal energy and state change to exchange with surfaces and across boundaries.

points.statement: Energy, charge, solid formation and changes of state concern how a substance stores energy and settles into a different condition.
points.name: Energy, charge, solid formation and changes of state concern how a substance stores energy and settles into a different condition.

support.rank_note: From energy and charge to phase and form change.

points.statement: Questions about energy and charge ask how a substance stores, exchanges and transports energy, charge or matter in solution and away from equilibrium.
points.name: Questions about energy and charge ask how a substance stores, exchanges and transports energy, charge or matter in solution and away from equilibrium.

support.rank_note: Kinds of energy and transport questions arranged by structure: energetics, electrical behaviour, solution medium, and transport processes.

points.statement: Solid-forming processes are those in which a solid phase emerges or separates out of a solution or melt.
points.name: Solid-forming processes are those in which a solid phase emerges or separates out of a solution or melt.

support.rank_note: Ordered by structure: ordered solid growth first, then general solid separation.

points.statement: Material behavior concepts describe how a substance's properties vary with direction or how it deteriorates through reaction with its environment.
points.name: Material behavior concepts describe how a substance's properties vary with direction or how it deteriorates through reaction with its environment.

support.rank_note: Ordered by structure: an intrinsic property first, then a degradation process.

points.statement: Changes of state or form describe a substance converting into a different physical or chemical condition.
points.name: Changes of state or form describe a substance converting into a different physical or chemical condition.

support.rank_note: Listed in structural order of change type.

points.statement: Interfaces, barriers, gradients, release and intermolecular forces concern how a substance exchanges matter and energy with its surroundings.
points.name: Interfaces, barriers, gradients, release and intermolecular forces concern how a substance exchanges matter and energy with its surroundings.

support.rank_note: From surfaces and barriers to gradients, release and molecular attraction.

points.statement: Questions about interfaces and uptake ask how a substance interacts with surfaces, other phases and ions, taking material in or holding it at a boundary.
points.name: Questions about interfaces and uptake ask how a substance interacts with surfaces, other phases and ions, taking material in or holding it at a boundary.

support.rank_note: Kinds of interface questions arranged by structure: surface science, bulk uptake, surface binding, and ionization of air.

points.statement: Barrier-passage processes separate a substance from a mixture by letting only certain components cross a membrane or filter.
points.name: Barrier-passage processes separate a substance from a mixture by letting only certain components cross a membrane or filter.

support.rank_note: Ordered by structure; no ranking implied.

points.statement: Gradient-driven processes ask how a substance moves or exchanges in response to concentration or charge differences.
points.name: Gradient-driven processes ask how a substance moves or exchanges in response to concentration or charge differences.

support.rank_note: Ordered by structure; no ranking implied.

points.statement: Movement and release phenomena describe how matter or energy gets through or out of a substance.
points.name: Movement and release phenomena describe how matter or energy gets through or out of a substance.

support.rank_note: Listed in structural order of movement type.

points.statement: Intermolecular interactions and structure concern how molecules attract one another, are arranged, and are probed.
points.name: Intermolecular interactions and structure concern how molecules attract one another, are arranged, and are probed.

support.rank_note: Listed in structural order from interaction to structure to probe.

points.title: Rates and mechanisms
points.statement: Rates and mechanisms is the question of how and how fast a substance reacts and is transformed, and by what pathway and driving agent.
points.name: Rates and mechanisms is the question of how and how fast a substance reacts and is transformed, and by what pathway and driving agent.

support.rank_note: From general reaction pathways to driving agents, bond rearrangements and organic processes.

points.statement: Questions about how a substance reacts ask by what pathway, how fast, and under what catalytic or light-driven influence a chemical change occurs.
points.name: Questions about how a substance reacts ask by what pathway, how fast, and under what catalytic or light-driven influence a chemical change occurs.

support.rank_note: Kinds of reaction questions arranged by structure: mechanism and catalysis, rate and dynamics, light-driven change, and the broad biochemical setting.

points.statement: Reaction-driving processes are ways a substance is made to react by an added agent such as a catalyst, water, light, or heat.
points.name: Reaction-driving processes are ways a substance is made to react by an added agent such as a catalyst, water, light, or heat.

support.rank_note: Ordered by the type of agent that drives the reaction.

points.statement: Transformation phenomena are changes in which a substance's own bonds or molecular structure are rearranged, as in organic chemistry, redox, and polymerization.
points.name: Transformation phenomena are changes in which a substance's own bonds or molecular structure are rearranged, as in organic chemistry, redox, and polymerization.

support.rank_note: Ordered by the kind of structural change to the substance.

points.statement: Process-focused subfields ask how organic substances react and are made, studying mechanisms, radical intermediates, deliberate synthesis and environmentally benign routes.
points.name: Process-focused subfields ask how organic substances react and are made, studying mechanisms, radical intermediates, deliberate synthesis and environmentally benign routes.

support.rank_note: Kinds of process-focused inquiry; ordered by structure, with no ranking.

points.title: Synthesis and analysis

points.name: Synthesis and analysis is the question of how a substance is made and how it is found, measured and characterised.

points.name: Assembly, analytical methods and forensic chemistry show how a substance is built and identified.

points.statement: Fields that ask how a substance is assembled or formed, through polymerisation, nanoscale synthesis or metal-carbon bonding.
points.name: Fields that ask how a substance is assembled or formed, through polymerisation, nanoscale synthesis or metal-carbon bonding.

points.name: Spectrometric, electrochemical and general instrumental methods answer what a substance is and how much of it is present by measuring its physical response.

points.name: Instrumental methods (excl. immunological and bioassay methods)

points.name: Quality assurance, chemometrics, traceability and metrological chemistry

points.name: Modelling, characterisation, informatics and the study of proteins, peptides and glycoconjugates ask what shape a biomolecule has and how it can be designed or predicted.

points.statement: Medicinal and biomolecular chemistry not elsewhere classified
points.name: Medicinal and biomolecular chemistry not elsewhere classified

points.statement: Imaging, measured properties, physical properties and energy probes show how a substance is quantified and characterised.
points.name: Imaging, measured properties, physical properties and energy probes show how a substance is quantified and characterised.

support.rank_note: From observation to measured and physical properties and probes.

points.statement: Questions about observation and definition ask how a substance is imaged at the molecular scale and how the field itself and its uncategorised topics are delimited.
points.name: Questions about observation and definition ask how a substance is imaged at the molecular scale and how the field itself and its uncategorised topics are delimited.

points.name: Molecular imaging (incl. electron microscopy and neutron diffraction)

points.statement: Measured properties are quantities that can be determined on a substance or solution.

points.statement: Solubility, specific gravity, and viscosity are kinds of physical property, each defined by a different question asked of a substance.

field_check.governing_thought: Chemistry is divided by the question asked of a substance, from what it is to how it is made or found: composition and identity, structure and bonding, equilibrium and energy, rates and mechanisms, and synthesis and analysis.
key_line: Composition and identity is the question of what a substance is, covering its general kind, its compound class and its role.
Structure and bonding is the question of how the atoms of a substance are arranged and held together, and how that arrangement shapes its response to light and theory.
Equilibrium and energy is the question of how a substance exchanges energy, charge and matter and settles between states, phases and surroundings.
Rates and mechanisms is the question of how and how fast a substance reacts and is transformed, and by what pathway and driving agent.
Synthesis and analysis is the question of how a substance is made and how it is found, measured and characterised.
field_check.note: Pillars overlap: intermolecular interactions (P3.2) belong in structure (P2); P2.3/P2.5 spectroscopy overlaps P5 analysis; P4.4 synthesis overlaps P5; P5.1 has a catch-all group.
